links.id: The id of the element the caret is in - a paragraph, a title, a poem. Give it an id so that a link can jump to it as #id.
links.idWhen: Available when the caret is in an element that can have an id.
links.href: Where the link or the picture points: #id of a place in this book, #id of one of the book's pictures, or a web address. Pick it from the list or type it.
links.hrefWhen: Available when the caret is in a link or on a picture.
links.sectionId: The id of the section the caret is in. Give a section an id so that links - a footnote's, a table of contents' - can jump to it as #id.
links.sectionIdWhen: Available when the caret is in a section.
links.imageTitle: The picture's title, shown under it in the text; FB2 writes it as the title attribute of the image.
links.imageTitleWhen: Available on a picture that stands on its own line; an inline picture has no title.
links.alt: The picture's alternative text, for readers that show no pictures; FB2 writes it as the alt attribute of the image.
links.hrefList: Open the list of the places and pictures the field can point to.

table.tableId: The id of the table the caret is in, so that a link can jump to it as #id.
table.tableStyle: The table's style: CSS declarations that readers may apply, for example border: 1px solid; FB2 writes it as the table's style attribute.
table.cellId: The id of the cell the caret is in, so that a link can jump to it as #id.
table.style: The style of the selected cells: CSS declarations, for example color: red; FB2 writes it as the cells' style attribute.
table.lang: The language of the selected cells' text, for example en or ru; FB2 writes it as xml:lang. Leave it empty to use the book's language.
table.colspan: How many columns the cell spans, 1 or more; FB2 writes it as colspan.
table.rowspan: How many rows the cell spans, 1 or more; FB2 writes it as rowspan.
table.trAlign: The horizontal alignment of the selected rows: left, center or right; FB2 writes it as the row's align.
table.tdAlign: The horizontal alignment of the text in the selected cells: left, center or right; FB2 writes it as align.
table.tdValign: The vertical alignment of the text in the selected cells: top, middle or bottom; FB2 writes it as valign.
table.whenTable: Available when the caret is in a table.
table.whenCell: Available when the caret is in a table cell.

view.language: The language of the editor's menus, dialogs and messages; System default follows the operating system. A change takes effect after a restart.
view.theme: Light, dark, or as the system is set. Colours of your own for the book's text, set below, stay as they are.
view.bodyFont: The font of the book's text in the Body view; Default font is the editor's own. It changes how the text looks on screen, never the book.
view.bodyFontSize: The size of the book's text in the Body view, in points, from 6 to 96.
view.textColor: The colour of the book's text in the Body view, as #rrggbb. Black on white follows the theme; any other colour replaces the theme's.
view.background: The colour behind the book's text in the Body view, as #rrggbb. White behind black text follows the theme; any other colour replaces the theme's.
view.fastMode: Shows the book without frames, backgrounds, colours and picture previews, so that very large books scroll faster; the book itself does not change. Also View > Fast Mode (F5).
view.sourceFont: The font of the Source view, where the book's XML is edited; Default font is the editor's own.
view.sourceFontSize: The size of the Source view's text, in points, from 6 to 96.
view.wrap: Long lines of the Source view continue on the next screen line instead of running off to the right.
view.showWhitespace: Shows the spaces and tabs of the Source view as faint marks.
view.syntaxHighlight: Colours the tags, attributes and text of the XML in the Source view.
view.lineNumbers: Numbers the lines of the Source view in its left margin.
view.showEol: Marks the end of every line of the Source view.
view.matchTags: With the caret on a tag of the Source view, highlights the tag that opens or closes it.
view.tagCompletion: While you type in the Source view, offers the tags, attributes and values the FB2 schema allows at that place.
view.useSpellchecker: Checks the spelling of the book's text with the dictionaries of the book's language.
view.highlightMisspelled: Underlines the words the dictionaries do not know with a wavy line.
view.baseDictionary: The dictionary of the book's language: always used.
view.extraDictionary: Also check the text with this dictionary, for books that mix languages.
view.customDictionary: The file of your own words: Add to dictionary writes there, and its words are never marked as misspelled.
view.dictionariesDefault: Look for dictionaries in the editor's own dictionaries folder.
view.dictionariesCustom: Look for dictionaries in a folder you choose, for example one shared with another program.
view.dictionariesPath: The folder with the dictionaries (.dic and .aff files) to use.
view.openDictionariesFolder: Opens the dictionaries folder in the file manager, to add or remove dictionaries.

other.encoding: The encoding a new book is saved in, and an opened one too unless Keep Encoding is on. UTF-8 suits every language.
other.keepEncoding: Saves an opened book in the encoding it was read in, instead of the default encoding.
other.keepBackup: Before a save replaces a file, keeps its previous version beside it as a .bak file.
other.restorePosition: Reopening a book puts the caret back where it was when you left the book.
other.switchKeyboardLayout: When a book opens, switches the keyboard to the layout chosen below, for example the language you type the book in.
other.keyboardLayout: The keyboard layout to switch to when a book opens.
other.askNonClearImage: Before Add > Image inserts a picture, asks whether to take it from a file or to insert an empty picture to fill in later.
other.insertClearImages: Without the question, Add > Image inserts an empty picture to fill in later instead of asking for a file.
other.imageFormat: The format a picture pasted from the clipboard is stored in: JPEG for photographs, PNG for drawings and pictures with transparent areas.
other.jpegQuality: The quality of pictures stored as JPEG, from 1 to 100: higher looks better, lower makes the book smaller.
other.nbsp: How a non-breaking space shows in the Body view; the book always keeps it as a non-breaking space.
other.openFromOutside: What happens when you open a book from outside the editor - from the file manager or another program - while a book is open in it.
other.versionCheck: How often the editor checks on the internet whether a newer version exists; Never keeps it fully offline.

scripts.default: Read your own scripts from the editor's own scripts folder.
scripts.path: The folder your own scripts are read from, besides the scripts that come with the editor.
scripts.open: Opens the scripts folder in the file manager.

genres.default: Read your own genre lists from the editor's own genres folder.
genres.path: The folder with your own genre lists, which add to or replace the standard one.
genres.open: Opens the genres folder in the file manager.

template.default: Read the template of new books from the editor's own template folder.
template.path: The folder with blank.fb2, the template every new book starts from.
template.open: Opens the template folder in the file manager.

words.rowCheck: Select the word, to remove it with Remove selected.
words.selectAll: Selects every word of the list, or none.
words.removeSelected: Removes the selected words from the exclusion list; the Words dialog counts them again.
words.newWord: A word the Words dialog leaves out of its list, for example a name that appears often: letters only, with at most one hyphen inside.
words.add: Adds the word to the exclusion list.
words.showExclusions: Shows the excluded words in the Words dialog too, marked, instead of leaving them out.

ai.modeFree: Use one of the free services of the bundled list: no registration and no key, with the limits each one states.
ai.service: The free service and model the assistant sends your requests to; its limits and terms are shown below.
ai.modeCustom: Use a service of your own choice - a hosted one with your key, or a model server on this computer.
ai.address: The address of the service's OpenAI-compatible interface, for example https://api.openai.com/v1, or http://127.0.0.1:11434/v1 for a server on this computer.
ai.key: Your key for the service; it is stored with the settings, sent only to this address and never written to a log. Leave it empty for a local server that needs none.
ai.revealKey: Shows or hides the key's characters.
ai.model: The model of your service that answers, for example gpt-4o-mini; type it or pick one after Fetch models.
ai.fetchModels: Asks the service for the list of models it offers, to pick one in the Model field.
ai.modeDisabled: Turns the assistant off: it leaves the menus, the toolbar and the shortcuts, and nothing of it is loaded.
ai.test: Sends a short test request to the service with these settings and reports whether it answers.
ai.editList: Opens your own service list file for editing; the first time, it is created as a copy of the bundled list.
ai.reloadList: Reads the service list files again after you edited them.
ai.revoke: Withdraws your agreement: before the next request to this service the editor asks again.
ai.effort: How much the model thinks before it answers: more effort gives better answers to hard tasks, slower and dearer; Model's default sends nothing.
ai.effortNone: The model offers no choice of thinking effort.

hotkeys.group: Shows the commands of this group, with their shortcuts.
hotkeys.capture: Click here and press the new shortcut, for example Ctrl+Shift+K; Assign then gives it to the selected command.
hotkeys.default: Gives the selected command back its default shortcut.
hotkeys.delete: Removes the shortcut from the selected command.
hotkeys.assign: Gives the shortcut you pressed to the selected command.

tabs.view: How the editor looks: language, theme, fonts and colours, the Source view and spelling.
tabs.other: Saving and opening books, pictures, non-breaking spaces, folders and the version check.
tabs.hotkeys: The keyboard shortcuts of every command.
tabs.words: The words the Words dialog leaves out of its list.
tabs.ai: The AI assistant: which service answers, or none at all.

dialog.dontAskAgain: Answer like this from now on, without asking again; the question can be turned back on in the Settings.

words.highlight: Mark the word: the buttons under Process highlighted act on the marked words.
words.replaced: Replace this word with its replacement when you press OK.
words.showExclusions: Shows the words of the exclusion list too, marked, or hides them.
words.highlightAll: Marks every word of the list.
words.setReplacedAll: Sets every word that has a replacement to be replaced when you press OK.
words.toExclusions: Moves the marked words to the exclusion list, so that this dialog leaves them out from now on.
words.setReplaced: Sets the marked words to be replaced with their replacements when you press OK.
words.invert: Marks the words that are not marked, and unmarks the others.
words.resetReplaced: The marked words will not be replaced.
words.currentWord: The word chosen in the list; Find shows it in the text.
words.replacement: The word to put in its place: Replace changes the occurrence found, OK every word set to be replaced.
words.find: Finds the word in the book's text, and the next occurrence on each further click.
words.replace: Replaces the occurrence found with the replacement.
words.editReplacement: The replacement of this word; Enter keeps it, Escape leaves it as it was.

spelling.notInDictionary: The word the dictionaries do not know; it is highlighted in the text.
spelling.changeTo: The spelling to put instead: pick a suggestion from the list or type it.
spelling.ignore: Leaves this occurrence as it is and goes on to the next unknown word.
spelling.ignoreAll: Leaves every occurrence of the word as it is until the editor closes.
spelling.change: Changes this occurrence to the spelling in Change To.
spelling.changeAll: Changes every occurrence of the word in the book to the spelling in Change To.
spelling.add: Adds the word to your own dictionary, so that it is never marked again.
spelling.undo: Takes back the last change made in this dialog.
spelling.dictionary: Check the text with this dictionary too: a word counts as known when any ticked dictionary knows it.
spelling.suggestion: A spelling the dictionaries know: a click puts it in Change To, a double-click changes the word to it.

find.findWhat: The text to look for; with Regular expression it is a pattern, for example colou?r.
find.wholeWords: Finds the text only as a whole word, not inside longer words.
find.matchCase: Finds the text only with the same capital and small letters.
find.regex: Reads the text to look for as a regular expression: . any character, \d a digit, * repeats what stands before it.
find.up: Searches from the caret towards the beginning of the book.
find.down: Searches from the caret towards the end of the book.
find.replaceWith: The text to put in place of each match; with Regular expression, $1 inserts the first group in brackets, $0 the whole match.

tableDialog.rows: How many rows the table has, from {{min}} to {{max}}.
tableDialog.columns: How many columns the table has, from {{min}} to {{max}}.
tableDialog.headerRow: Makes the first row a header row: its cells become th, which readers show as headings.
tableDialog.headerColumn: Makes the first cell of every row a header cell (th), for tables whose rows have names.

saveFile.encoding: The encoding the book is saved in: UTF-8 suits every language, a legacy code page only the languages it covers.
saveFile.zip: Packs the saved book into a ZIP archive, which many readers and libraries accept; the book inside keeps its name.

customizeToolbar.available: The buttons you can add: select one and press Add; Separator adds a dividing line.
customizeToolbar.current: The toolbar's buttons in their order: select one to remove it or to move it up or down.

about.basedOn: The licence, the copyright and the contributors of FictionBook Editor 2.7, which this editor is based on.
about.openLogFolder: Opens the folder of the editor's error log in the file manager, for example to attach the log to a bug report.

views.description: The book's description: its title, authors, genres, annotation, cover and the other data a library shows.
views.body: The book's text as it reads, with its sections, titles, poems and pictures, to edit it.
views.source: The book's XML, to edit it directly; the other views follow when you leave it.

archive.filter: Shows only the books of the archive whose name contains this text.

link.href: Where the link points: #id of a place in this book, for example #note1, or a web address such as https://example.com.

openElsewhere.remember: Answer like this for every book opened from outside; Settings > Other can change it.

importDescription.entry: Takes this part of the other book's description into this book; untick it to keep this book's own.

run.cancel: Stops the running script or the assistant's request.

ai.settingsLink: Opens Settings → AI assistant, to choose the service that answers.
ai.input: Your instruction or question for the assistant, about the selected text or the book; Enter sends it, Shift+Enter starts a new line.
ai.stop: Stops the request: the assistant stops answering.
ai.clear: Clears the conversation, so that the next request starts afresh.
ai.popupInput: What the assistant should do with the selected text, or your question; Enter sends it, Shift+Enter starts a new line.
ai.continue: Moves this request and its answer to the assistant's panel, to go on there.
ai.enableLink: Opens Settings → AI assistant, to turn the assistant on.
ai.disabledInput: The assistant is turned off: turn it on in Settings → AI assistant to give it an instruction.
ai.disabledSend: Sends the instruction to the assistant. Available when the assistant is turned on in Settings → AI assistant.
ai.disabledClear: Clears the conversation. Available when the assistant is turned on in Settings → AI assistant.
ai.disabledUndo: Undoes the assistant's last change to the book. Available when the assistant is turned on in Settings → AI assistant.
ai.proposalAuthor: The author line, written as the first comment of the script the assistant proposes; clear it to write none.

titleInfo.bookTitle: The book's title, as readers and libraries show it.

date.text: When the book was written, as it should read, for example 2026 or spring 2026.

srcTitleInfo.bookTitle: For a translation: the title of the original book.
srcTitleInfo.lang: The language of the original book.

description.keywords: Words a library can find the book by, separated by commas.
description.lang: The language of the book's text, for example en, ru or uk; the spelling check uses its dictionaries.
description.srcLang: For a translation: the language the book was translated from.

date.text: When this FB2 file was made, as it should read, for example 15 March 2026.

documentInfo.programUsed: The programs this FB2 file was made with.
documentInfo.srcUrls: A web address the book's text was taken from.
documentInfo.srcOcr: Who scanned and recognised the printed book, if it was.
documentInfo.id: The unique id of this FB2 file; libraries tell the versions of one book apart by it. Keep it when you make a new version.
documentInfo.version: The version of this FB2 file, for example 1.0; raise it with every new release of the file.

date.text: The date as it should read, for example 2026 or March 2026.
date.value: The same date for programs, as YYYY-MM-DD, for example 2026-03-15.

description.name: The name of the series the book belongs to, for example The Lord of the Rings.
description.number: The book's number in the series, for example 2.

genres.match: How well the genre fits the book, in percent; empty means 100.

description.middleName: The person's middle name or patronymic.
description.nickname: The person's nickname or pen name; a person without a first and a last name needs one.
description.homePages: A web page of the person, for example https://example.com.
description.emails: An e-mail address of the person.
description.id: The person's id in a library catalogue, if there is one.

publishInfo.bookName: The title of the printed book this text comes from.
publishInfo.publisher: The publisher of the printed book.
publishInfo.city: The city where the printed book was published.
publishInfo.year: The year the printed book was published.
publishInfo.isbn: The ISBN of the printed book, for example 978-3-16-148410-0.

customInfo.infoType: The kind of the extra information, as a short name of your own.

description.role: The person's part in the book, for example illustrator or editor; it is written as a custom-info entry.
description.genreFilter: Shows only the genres whose name or code contains this text.
description.genreList: The genres of the list: pick one and press OK, or double-click it.
description.coverHref: The picture shown as the book's cover, chosen among the book's pictures.

body.tab: Shows this body of the book - the main text or, for example, the notes.
body.moreBefore: Shows the sections before the ones on screen; the view holds a window of sections, so that large books stay quick.
body.moreAfter: Shows the sections after the ones on screen; the view holds a window of sections, so that large books stay quick.

source.foldLevel: The nesting level the Collapse and Expand buttons beside it act on: 1 folds the outermost elements, higher levels deeper ones.
